claim: Total stock market return decomposes exactly (identity, not estimate) into dividend-price ratio x earnings-growth-rate x price-earnings-ratio-growth-rate, and forecasting these three components separately produces far higher out-of-sample explanatory power than forecasting the aggregate return directly.
stance_target: durability-based decomposition of earnings (query Phase 3) is methodologically superior to blending into one EPS/one P/E
scope_conditions: US aggregate stock market, 1927-2007 sample, monthly and annual (non-overlapping) frequencies only
quoted_support: 1 + Rt+1 = (1+GMt+1)(1+GEt+1)(1+DPt+1)... forecasting separately the components of stock market returns delivers out-of-sample R-squares significantly higher than traditional predictive regressions.
numbers: out-of-sample R-squared: 1.32% (monthly, div+earnings only) vs -1.78% to 0.69% (traditional regression, monthly)
13.43% (annual, div+earnings only) vs -17.57% to 7.54% (traditional regression, annual)

claim: Price-earnings multiple mean-reversion is slow, taking up to nearly 10 years to revert to its fitted/fundamental value, so it does not average out within a 2-5 year holding period.
stance_target: over 2-5y, multiple change is a durable, non-mean-reverted exposure rather than noise that cancels out (query research question 8)
scope_conditions: US aggregate market P/E ratio regressed on macro variables (SVAR, term spread, T-bill rate), 1927-2007
quoted_support: the realized multiple reverts to the fitted value... the reversion is quite slow and at times takes almost 10 years.

claim: The sum-of-the-parts decomposition contains no separate treatment of buyback yield or share-count reduction as a return component; buyback effects are implicitly absorbed into the per-share earnings-growth term.
stance_target: how much buybacks contribute to 2-5y total return as a distinct, isolable driver (query implicit question 14)
scope_conditions: methodological scope of the SOP framework itself; absence noted, not measured
quoted_support: we decompose the total return of the stock market index into dividend yield and capital gains... [capital gains] = growth in price-earnings ratio x growth in earnings per share

claim: No holding-period-specific (2-year, 3-year, or 5-year) return decomposition exists in the sum-of-the-parts literature; only monthly and annual (non-overlapping) frequencies are reported.
stance_target: direct empirical answer to the query's 2-5y-horizon-specific research question 8
scope_conditions: audited absence — searched the full paper text for horizon/holding-period terms and found none beyond monthly/annual
quoted_support: We now turn to the annual stock market return forecasts results in panel B of Table 2. We use non-overlapping returns to avoid the concerns with the measurement of R-squares with overlapping returns pointed out by Valkanov (2003)...
